elements.problem: No rule encodes the 'seen promptly' criteria box. Parts missing: BP ≥ 180/110; systolic BP < 80; pregnant with BP ≥ 140/90; pulse irregular; pulse ≥ 100; pulse < 50; temperature ≥ 38°C; respiratory rate ≥ 30 (only present via the red box); glucose < 3; glucose < 4 if diabetic; glucose ≥ 11.1; SpO2 < 92% at rest; SpO2 drop to < 87% on exertion (not representable). The language has no priority level below Urgent, so encoding would have to be at Urgent (overstating) or omitted; but nothing records the decision, and the measure tasks above have no consumer that acts on these thresholds.

summary: The red box is fully and faithfully encoded: all 20 criteria appear in a single Urgent priority rule with correct and/or logic and a matching check list, and the conditional glucose check is a measure task. The most consequential gap is that the 'seen promptly' threshold box (BP, pulse, temperature, glucose, SpO2 cut-offs) is not encoded at all, likely because the grammar has no level below Urgent. Monitoring-schedule boxes are partially encoded as measure tasks, with tests and visit timing not representable and the hypertension trigger lacking a Known-present form.
